messages:
Asha (Support): FYI — ACME raised a subtle but recurring complaint after we rolled rw-infer-2.3 yesterday. They say answers now contain more hedging and extra explanatory sentences (e.g., 'It might be' / 'I'm not 100% sure' / 'It depends on...'), and a few replies are 20–30% longer. They supplied side-by-side examples. :eyes:

Asha (Support): Customer quote / repro (redacted):
--- prompt ---
User: "Summarize the main regulatory risks for deploying an LLM in the EU."
--- before (rw-infer-2.2) ---
"Key regulatory risks: data residency, GDPR consent, DPIA requirements, and vendor due diligence. Recommend mapping data flows and running a DPIA."
--- after (rw-infer-2.3) ---
"I'm not an attorney, but it might be important to consider data residency and GDPR consent. It probably depends on how you process personal data and vendor contracts. You may also want to look at DPIAs and vendor due diligence, though that can vary by case."

Asha (Support): They say the newer output reads less definitive and adds hedges/qualifiers even for factual lists. They filed a support ticket and escalated to us when a product PM flagged UX regressions. Ticket ref: ACME-2247. Request: can we confirm whether this is an instruction-following/regression change or a config rollout?

Jon (Customer Success): Thanks for flagging. ACME is on Dedicated with a pinned model alias but allowed minor auto-updates (we pushed 2.3 last night). They attached a few dozen examples where 'maybe/might/probably' frequency jumped. CS metrics: customer-reported NPS hit on recent answers. They want either rollback or a mitigation (short-term: system prompt override / param to reduce hedging).

Luca (Eng-ML): I'll take a look. Can you paste one request_id and the exact model string? Also any headers (temperature, top_p, system prompt)?

Asha (Support): Sure — sample request id: req_0a9c3f. Model header: "model: rw-infer-2.3", params: {"temperature":0.2, "top_p":0.95, "system":"You are a helpful assistant."} (customer didn't set a verbosity param).

Luca (Eng-ML): Initial notes: deployment bot shows rw-infer-2.3 rolled at 2026-03-12T02:11Z and was promoted from canary -> all within 1 hour. deploy-bot below.

deploy-bot: rw-infer-2.3 promoted to production (rollout id r-20260312-0211) :rocket:

Luca (Eng-ML): Running quick diff on eval set vs 2.2. I'm seeing a ~18% increase in average tokens per response on our regulatory prompts and a big uptick in hedge-word frequency ("might","probably","depends","I'm not sure"). Also see a small increase in perplexity for some system-following prompts. Pasting commands I used:

```
# pull sample outputs
cat samples/regulatory_prompts.txt | xargs -I{} curl -s -X POST https://internal-api/redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rw-infer-2.2","prompt":"{}"}' > out_2.2.txt
cat samples/regulatory_prompts.txt | xargs -I{} curl -s -X POST https://internal-api/redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rw-infer-2.3","prompt":"{}"}' > out_2.3.txt
python3 tools/style_diff.py out_2.2.txt out_2.3.txt --metrics hedge_word_freq avg_tokens
```

Luca (Eng-ML): style_diff output (summary): hedge_word_freq: 2.1% (2.2) -> 9.4% (2.3); avg_tokens: 48 -> 57. So it's not just one prompt.

Priya (Product): Interesting. Did any of the model tuning experiments change the instruction-following loss or safety/hedging classifier? Any inference-stage biasing or decaying of system prompt?

Luca (Eng-ML): Checking CLs now. There's a change in the instruction-tuning checkpoint we merged last week (internal ref: IT-457). The change added a small penalty on overconfident assertions to reduce hallucinations (team rationale: reduce false factual definitiveness). That fits the symptom: model is being nudged to hedge more. I want to verify the magnitude though — the CLI flag for safety_bias was unintentionally set from -0.3 -> -0.6 in the 2.3 config, doubling the effect.

Asha (Support): So it's a deliberate safety tweak that overshot? Can we revert quickly for Dedicated customers who report UX impact?

Luca (Eng-ML): For hosted we can rollback rollout to 2.2 for account groups; for Dedicated it's trickier but ACME is on a non-strict pin so we can push a hotfix to restore safety_bias to previous value and roll new model build (2.3.1) or provide a runtime param to disable the penalty per request. 

Priya (Product): Short-term mitigation options I see:
- Offer ACME a per-account flag that sets `safety_bias: -0.3` to match 2.2 behavior (quick config toggle)
- Create a system_prompt override sample that reduces hedging (e.g., add "Answer concisely and avoid uncertain language unless necessary.")
- Rollback to 2.2 for ACME (if they want immediate fix)
Long-term: add unit tests for 'hedge word frequency' in our eval suite and a gating rule preventing >5% delta on that metric without PM sign-off.

Jon (Customer Success): ACME prefers not to be rolled back unless we can guarantee no other regressions. They asked for a runtime param or system prompt. They want an ETA and honest comms.

Luca (Eng-ML): Action plan from Eng: 1) push rollback config to match 2.2 safety_bias for ACME by EOD (will use per-account override); 2) build 2.3.1 with safety_bias -0.3 and run full evals, target deploy 2.3.1 in 48 hours; 3) add style metric to CI. I'll open ENG-ISSUE-892 and link sample diffs.

Asha (Support): I'll reply to ACME with the plan and offer the system prompt override they can try immediately. Can you paste a recommended system prompt?

Luca (Eng-ML): Recommended system prompt to reduce hedging: "You are a knowledgeable assistant. Provide direct, concise answers. Avoid hedging phrases such as 'might', 'probably', or 'I'm not sure' unless the user asks for uncertainty. If a definitive answer isn't possible, state the specific missing information needed." Use with low temperature (<=0.2).

Priya (Product): I'll add the monitoring rule request to the backlog and tag it P1 for regressions that impact customer UX. Also will prepare a short customer-facing note describing why the safety tweak was applied and our rollback/mitigation steps.

deploy-bot: rollback config r-20260312-0211 -> applied for account-group ACME (override id ov-ACME-001) :white_check_mark:

Asha (Support): Thanks everyone — I'll update the ticket and send the prompt + short instructions. Will follow up after ACME tests. Assigning owners: Luca -> ENG-ISSUE-892, Priya -> PM communication, Jon -> customer comms.

Jon (Customer Success): Thanks — ACME replied faster than I expected, they want the system prompt now. Will share feedback once they test. :thumbsup:
notes: thread documents should include entire thread as a single string with messages prefixed by sender names
